title: Export Matches Table
description: The CSV export exists so a dispatcher can take the tracking table offline into a spreadsheet — but it always exports unpaginated (capped at 100 rows), unlike the on-screen table. Confirm the export's content genuinely matches the underlying data, filters included, even when the live table view is paginated down to a handful of rows at a time.
successCondition: Book 5 shipments as a dispatcher-visible set (or as a dispatcher/admin account directly). GET /api/tracking?status=booked&pageSize=2&page=1 (a small page) returns only 2 items. GET /api/tracking/export.csv?status=booked (same filter, no pagination params — always capped at 100 rows per docs/api/tracking.md) returns a CSV whose data rows include all 5 (or however many actually match status=booked) shipment ids, with the header exactly id,status,origin,destination,weightKg,distanceKm,priceCents,currency,createdAt, and each row's values match the corresponding shipment's fields from the JSON listing exactly (distanceKm formatted to one decimal place).
hints: The CSV export ignores page/pageSize entirely even if you pass them — docs/api/tracking.md says it's "always unpaginated, capped at 100 rows" — don't expect the small page size from your table view call to affect the export.
distanceKm in the CSV is formatted with toFixed(1) — a raw floating-point comparison against the JSON's unformatted distanceKm will need a formatting-aware comparison, not exact string equality.
